design.decision: Bid more aggressively and play to set the opponents, since some of their winners are gone.
design.opponent: Revealed at Opening, because it changes their cards. They see which of their cards became [2]s before bidding and adjust, so it is input randomness, not hidden interference.
design.rationale: Any team would buy it before knowing its build, because a weaker opposing hand helps every plan. It changes who wins tricks without touching your own cards, so it never harms a Nil or Low Cards hand. It resolves before bidding, so it is neither an information effect nor randomness after bidding begins.
design.draftText: Opening: Three cards the opponents hold become [2]s
design.hooks: Opening changes gain a `whose` field (`team` by default, or `opponents`) that samples cards from the opposing pair's hands instead of your team's. The text says 'the opponents hold', and touchesOpponents becomes true.

critic.concerns: The only sigil that changes the opponents' hand: it can feed their nil and [2] payoffs, and degrading their bought cards every round may feel bad, though they see it before bidding.
